Proxy

Allowed formats: ip:port, ip:port:user:pass, or URL form like socks5://user:pass@ip:port. Plain lines default to HTTP proxy.

Message UI build 2026-10-14b · 4 chat modes · browser mode

One line equals one bot message step. Line 1 is first message, line 2 is second reply, line 3 is third reply, and so on.

Select Chat Mode:
Each new line is the next message the bot sends for that conversation step. Template format: {hello|hi|helo}{how|hw}.
Loads multiple chat sequence files (.txt) from a folder. The bot picks a random sequence per user.
TXT data is initialized when EVAChat Flow starts.
EVAChat Flow is a stateful TXT-driven conversation engine (no API; for AI chat use the API Chat mode). Edit data/eva_chat/input/ for user-message triggers and data/eva_chat/output/ for reply pools. The same file name connects a trigger category to its replies (see docs/CHAT_ENGINE_MAPPING.md). Fill the Usernames list: share_snap.txt uses %username%. Changes are loaded when the bot starts.
API Chat — the AI writes every line; the built-in director decides the funnel (interest tiers, when the snap is shared, hint / direct / no-snap chats). The snap handle is never written by the AI — it comes from data\api_chat\snap_share.txt; usernames from the list below, one per stranger from a shuffled deck.
Funnel rules (when the snap is shared, % of chats with no snap, hint-first %) are not dashboard settings — edit ONE file: cmd\apitest\config_rules.json (used by the bot and by the apitest lab), then restart the bot. The Test API result and the start log show the rules that were loaded and from which file. (Only if the project folder is not found does the bot fall back to data\api_chat\config_rules.json.)
Use %username% anywhere in message templates to insert one random Snap / Telegram handle.

Browser

Select the browser backend and profile used for login capture, or turn on Browser mode to keep the window open and chat through it.

If the saved login is missing or expired, the selected backend will open the login browser.
Off = the bot works exactly as before (browser only for login, then API calls from the app).
On = one visible browser window per account opens at Start and stays open until you press Stop: login, matching and every message happen through that window (real cookies, real browser, no websocket). If the session expires the bot waits for you to log in again in the window. Stop saves the session (login_info.json) and closes the window, so the next Start logs in automatically.
Notes: Headless is ignored in this mode (the window must be visible). Each account = one Chrome window (about 300–500 MB RAM), so use it for a few accounts. The proxy is picked per window at Start and stays fixed. New replies are picked up by the normal cycle (no realtime push in this version).
